request.spec:
A steward can cancel a person's last statement (a button on the row; STATEMENT_CANCELLED
name=<name> due-total=<the cancelled statement's due-total>; anyone else, or a person with no
statement, is refused with an error on the row). The claims that statement bound become live
again; a figure bound by a statement before it is not restored. The statement count goes down by
one, and the row shows the statement before it (or nothing).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can cancel a person's last statement (a button on the row; STATEMENT_CANCELLED
name=<name> due-total=<the cancelled statement's due-total>; anyone else, or a person with no
statement, is refused with an error on the row). The claims that statement bound become live
again; a figure bound by a statement before it is not restored. The statement count goes down by
one, and the row shows the statement before it (or nothing).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text: An old background watcher I had left running to wait for the first test run hit its time limit and was stopped. It never exited because its `pgrep -f "bin/e2e"` check most likely matched its own command line. Nothing depended on it, so I haven't restarted it. The last full `bin/e2e` run had already finished with all 4 tests passing.
